correctness.rationale: One-point extensions over a fixed induced position F ask for an ordinary point or an admissible root in a specified active class, or for either colour in a fresh class. For rank ≥t each active class must actually have a host root: either already marked or required by a legal root challenge. An ordinary move in that class requires capacity t by induction at t−1. Fresh moves reduce to the untouched union U, since the other active classes play no role in these options. Conversely old moves preserve the relative conditions at t−1, and for fresh moves the winning responses in U combine with those conditions. At t=1 the two fresh colours can be realized independently and the active classes require a root and one spare ordinary point; this starts the induction for (R). For t≥2 a fresh ordinary challenge forces a rooted class with at least t ordinary points and remaining rank ≥t−1; the same class can answer a fresh root challenge, proving sufficiency. Peeling thresholds t down to 2 can use the largest rooted capacities: substituting a larger unchosen class leaves a rooted class of positive ordinary capacity behind, so the terminal rank-one requirement is preserved. The unused rooted and ordinary witnesses give b≥t and u_t+z≥1. Equality in the resulting size sum requires exact peeled capacities and a two-point terminal pair of different colours, together or apart. This gives exactly the two isomorphism types, also at t=1. Adding points to a fixed induced host cannot decrease rank because the old strategy remains available; the formula at exact order n follows, including the empty host.
residual_risks: The independent replay covered 734 unlabelled hosts of orders 0–9 and all 220,777 marked subsets across them. It compared exact ranks and found exactly two minimum forms at each of orders 2, 5 and 9. The all-size result is proved by the induction and exchange, not by the replay.

The proof is for induced substructures with at most one root per class; marking only ordinary points in a rooted host class does not turn it into a rootless host class. Neither arbitrary colour multiplicities nor infinite-host ranks are classified.

value.rationale: The problem asks for a complete evaluation of a motivated extension-game invariant on a natural hereditary class. The answer determines the rank at every marked position as well as the sharp minimum and both extremal configurations; it exposes exactly how an unrooted class contributes at the last step without substituting for a rooted class earlier. This is more information than an isolated rank threshold or an uncoloured restatement.
residual_risks: The contribution is a finite-class structural rank calculation, not a new general theory of Fraïssé ranks or a result for infinite hosts.
